evidence.verdictBefore:
Prediction · Within this example’s touchdown limits
Contact speed, distance from target, tilt and impact energy meet the limits entered for this example. Watch the continuation for sliding or tipping; this does not certify a real landing.

evidence.verdictAfter:
Prediction · Landing misses this example’s limits
Too fast up/down: 23.13 m/s at contact, above your 2 m/s limit. The engine did not remove enough vertical speed before contact.
Too much sideways speed: 10.53 m/s, above your 1 m/s limit. There is still sliding motion to remove.
Missed the target: 89.53 m away, outside your 20 m target radius. More sideways braking or a different start position may help.
Impact energy 1,509,784.19 J reaches the example's 100,000 J breakup threshold. Expect illustrative fragments, not a reconstruction of real structural damage.

evidence.feedback:
Changed Thrust

16000 → 4000. The maximum engine push. Too little push cannot slow the fall in time. Assisted guidance can throttle down; manual guidance uses full thrust, so too much push or a long burn can make the vehicle climb again.

Predicted up/down contact speed: 0.51 → 23.13 m/s. Target distance: 7.49 → 89.53 m.

Playback reset and paused. Press Play to watch the changed setup. These are calculated comparisons, not proof that one input alone caused a real-world outcome.
